attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation gives an exact upper-bound falsifier class, but it does not prove that arbitrary small circuits for H_N factor through low-arity tuple transcripts. The remaining source obligation is a genuine unrestricted-circuit lower bound or a non-natural theorem ruling out all residual systems and all non-factored circuits.
steps: Fix the generated-OR carrier H_N from the previous cycles with M_N=N^q generated SAT instances of length L=(log N)^d and batch generator size N^{rho+o(1)}.
Choose r=N^s arity-t predicates P_i. After computing the batch B_N(x), enumerate all M_N^t ordered tuples and OR the predicate outputs to obtain transcript bits z_i(x).
The transcript circuit size is at most N^{rho+o(1)} plus r M_N^t N^{alpha+o(1)}, giving exponent max{rho,s+tq+alpha}.
Apply an aggregator A_N of size N^gamma to obtain S_N(x). If a residual circuit E_N of size N^lambda computes H_N(x) xor S_N(x), then H_N is computed by S_N xor E_N.
Thus any claimed source lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} must imply theta_t>=1+epsilon-o(1) for every such tuple-feature residual system.

Independently, if SAT has n^c-size circuits, substituting them into the M_N polylogarithmic generated queries gives C(H_N)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}, so the target bridge remains valid when max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: It is route-level progress only. A valid H_N lower bound above N^{1+epsilon} is still unproved, and proving it by a natural dense property would trigger the natural-proofs obstruction.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: tuple-feature residual gate

assumptions: q,rho,epsilon are fixed constants and max{rho,q}<1+epsilon is separated by Omega(1).
The batch generator B_N is shared once; tuple enumeration costs M_N^t=N^{tq}.
Predicate, aggregator, and residual circuits are nonuniform but receive only their specified inputs.
The source lower bound is against unrestricted Boolean circuits for H_N, not against a restricted tuple-feature model.
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=OR_{j<M_N} SAT(B_N(x)_j), where |x|=N, M_N=N^q, B_N outputs M_N formulas of length L=(log N)^d with d>1, and B_N has nonuniform circuit size N^{rho+o(1)}.
target object: SAT notin P/poly, obtained route-theoretically from a general-circuit lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} under the generated-query substitution interface.

controlled interface: hypothetical SAT circuits are substituted only into the generated polylogarithmic queries; source-side falsifiers are nonuniform tuple-feature transcripts followed by an aggregator and a residual correction circuit.

target-preserving condition: max{rho,q}<1+epsilon with a fixed positive margin, L=(log N)^d for d>1, no N-dependent advice except the circuits being counted, and no exhaustive SAT lookup hidden inside the source audit.
A tuple-feature system has arity t, r=N^s predicates P_i on t generated formulas, predicate cost N^{alpha+o(1)}, aggregator cost N^gamma, and residual E_N=H_N xor S_N of cost N^lambda.
The transcript bit z_i(x) is OR over all ordered t-tuples of generated formulas of P_i(B_N(x)_{j_1},...,B_N(x)_{j_t}); S_N(x)=A_N(z_1(x),...,z_r(x)).

equations.label: tuple_feature_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when the batch generator is shared once, tuple features are densely enumerated over all M_N^t tuples, and E_N exactly computes H_N xor S_N.

equations.label: subthreshold_falsifier_exponent
equations.valid_when: Valid when all exponent inequalities have a fixed margin and polynomially many additive circuit components are absorbed into the maximum exponent.

equations.label: target_substitution_bridge
equations.valid_when: Applies after SAT circuits are substituted only into length L=(log N)^d generated queries, so L^c=N^{o(1)} for each fixed c.

equations.label: route_magnification_consequence
equations.valid_when: Requires an eventually valid unrestricted-circuit lower bound for the named carrier and fixed target-preserving parameters q,rho,epsilon with positive slack.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Exhibit t,s,alpha,gamma,lambda with theta_t<1+epsilon and a valid residual E_N; that is a concrete falsifier for the proposed H_N lower bound, not a proof of SAT lower bounds.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Bridge-preserving falsifier lemma: it leaves the target substitution theorem intact while enlarging the source lower-bound obligation from local features to low-arity tuple features plus residual correction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the generated-OR SAT carrier, any low-cost arity-t tuple-feature transcript plus a low-cost residual circuit is a concrete subthreshold upper bound for H_N. Therefore a valid N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound must defeat every such tuple-feature residual system below the threshold, not only single-formula selectors or separators.

assumptions: The transcript is implemented by explicit OR enumeration over tuples.
The feature count exponent s and predicate exponent alpha are nonnegative constants.
No unproved compression of the tuple scan is assumed.
definitions: dense tuple transcript: each feature bit scans all ordered t-tuples from the M_N=N^q generated formulas.
threatening arity: an arity t for which the transcript enumeration exponent can remain below 1+epsilon after adding feature-count and predicate exponents.
shortcut exception: a circuit computes the same tuple statistic without paying M_N^t, for example through generator algebra or a sparse tuple selector.

equations.label: dense_arity_threat_window
equations.valid_when: Valid when q is positive and each transcript bit is computed by dense enumeration over generated formula tuples.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a sparse tuple selector or algebraic batch computation with exponent below tq; then the dense cutoff is not a valid audit for that carrier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quantitative pruning of source audits: it identifies exactly which tuple arities must be checked before the generated-OR route can claim a valid source lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Under dense tuple enumeration, only arities t with s+tq+alpha<1+epsilon can threaten the N^{1+epsilon} source threshold. Hence for fixed q>0 the direct tuple-feature falsifier search has a finite arity cutoff; higher arities require a sparse selector, convolutional shortcut, or another non-dense interface to matter.

assumptions: Standard pseudorandom-function assumptions are used only as a natural-proofs warning.
The tuple-feature residual condition is currently a nonuniform circuit lower-bound obligation, not an explicit constructive property.
definitions: relativizing part: the substitution SAT-circuit-to-H_N-circuit implication treats SAT labels as an oracle table for generated queries.
non-natural requirement: the source lower-bound proof should not define a large constructive property containing H_N and excluding all N^{1+epsilon} circuits.
scope limitation: this lemma is a barrier audit, not an impossibility theorem for the generated-OR carrier.

equations.label: naturalness_warning_shape
equations.valid_when: Valid as a barrier diagnostic when the proposed lower-bound proof proceeds by a large efficiently checkable property of N-bit truth tables.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the only proposed proof of the H_N lower bound is a large constructive property, quarantine the route as natural-proof blocked rather than merely difficult.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier interaction certificate: it prevents advertising the residual audit as progress toward P != NP unless the source proof is shown non-natural, nonrelativizing, or explicitly outside the known barrier scope.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The target bridge is syntactic and relativizing; the hard source assertion must therefore be non-natural or otherwise outside standard natural-proof templates. A proof that H_N avoids all subthreshold tuple-feature residual systems by a dense, efficiently decidable largeness property of truth tables would collide with the natural-proofs obstruction under pseudorandom function assumptions.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if every plausible H_N lower-bound proof becomes a large constructive natural property, or if sparse tuple shortcuts collapse the dense arity cutoff for the intended carrier.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only after proving a non-natural unrestricted lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} that defeats all tuple-feature residual systems while preserving max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.
control_decision.reason: The branch produced a concrete bridge-preserving falsifier lemma with named source model, target consequence, and threshold exponents. It is valid route-level progress, but the unrestricted source lower bound remains open.

dependency_updates.description: Add arity-t tuple-feature transcripts and residual correction to the generated-OR source audit; the threshold exponent is max{rho,s+tq+alpha,gamma,lambda}.
For dense tuple enumeration, only t<(1+epsilon-s-alpha)/q can be a direct subthreshold falsifier; larger t matters only through shortcuts.
The SAT-to-H_N substitution theorem remains unchanged: SAT in SIZE(n^c) yields H_N in SIZE(N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}).
A contribution-making source lower bound must now beat low-arity tuple features, aggregators, residual circuits, and non-factored unrestricted circuits.
The bridge itself is relativizing; any source proof by a large constructive property is natural-proof suspect and must be certified non-natural or quarantined.

falsifiers: tuple-feature falsifier: some arity t system has max{rho,s+tq+alpha,gamma,lambda}<1+epsilon and an exact or low-cost residual for H_N.
sparse-tuple falsifier: the carrier admits a selector or algebraic shortcut computing the same tuple transcript below the dense M_N^t exponent.
target-window falsifier: max{rho,q}>=1+epsilon, so the SAT-circuit substitution no longer contradicts the claimed source lower bound.
lookup falsifier: L or the generated range is small enough that SAT labels on the relevant range are nonuniformly tabulated below N^{1+epsilon}.
nonuniform-leakage falsifier: advice encodes a hitting family for positive bags or a separator for negative bags with subthreshold residual correction.
natural-proof falsifier: the only available source proof is a large constructive property of truth tables, leaving the route blocked under standard PRF-based natural-proofs barriers.
model-mismatch falsifier: the tuple lower bound is proved only for restricted circuits while the target bridge requires unrestricted P/poly substitution.

Batch generator size exponent rho and query-count exponent q remain below 1+epsilon, preserving the target bridge.

The carrier remains H_N(x)=OR_j SAT(phi_j), but S_N(x)=OR_{i,j} P_2(phi_i,phi_j) is intended to match H_N on most or all inputs.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: There is no target-preserving theorem converting polynomial Boolean circuit size into sublinear balanced communication or low matrix rank. The threshold collapses to the maximum rank sqrt(N).
steps: Fix m=2r and a balanced partition pi of SAT_m's input bits.
Try to prove rank_F(M_pi(SAT_m)) > m^k and infer SAT_m notin SIZE(m^k).
Use the standard bridge rank_F(M_pi(g)) <= 2^{D_pi(g)} for functions with deterministic communication cost D_pi(g).
The needed target bound would be D_pi(g) <= O(log m) for every g in SIZE(m^k), or equivalently rank_F(M_pi(g)) <= poly(m).
This target bound is false: EQ_r under the same partition has rank 2^r and has Boolean circuit size O(m).
The only valid conclusion from a rank lower bound is separation from classes with separately proved low balanced communication, not from full SIZE(poly).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation proves a restricted communication-rank transfer and a falsifier for the full-circuit route. It gives no lower bound for SAT against polynomial-size Boolean circuits and no evidence for P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: balanced matrix rank gate

assumptions: Field F is fixed and explicitly named; F_2 and R are the main audit cases.
The rank certificate is computed from the full truth table of f_m, so constructivity is measured in poly(N) time for N=2^m.
For the transfer half, every function in the named target class has a deterministic balanced protocol or equivalent rank-one decomposition of the stated cost.
For the full-SIZE refutation, the target includes ordinary fan-in-two Boolean circuits with NOT gates and polynomial size.
definitions: source object: for an m-bit Boolean slice f_m and a fixed balanced partition pi=(X,Y), define the communication matrix M_pi(f_m) with rows x in {0,1}^r and columns y in {0,1}^r, where r=floor(m/2).
target object: nonuniform SIZE(m^k), or a restricted class T_s whose functions have balanced deterministic communication cost at most c_T(m,s) under the same partition.
controlled interface: a rank lower bound transfers only through a certified upper bound rank_F(M_pi(g)) <= R_T(m,s) for every target function g, with the same field, partition, and input length.
target-preserving condition: pi, F, m, and s=m^k are fixed before seeing the candidate hard slice, and no advice may choose a partition that hides high-rank easy functions.

equations.label: matrix_definition
equations.valid_when: Valid when the input slice length and balanced partition are fixed before evaluating the rank certificate.

equations.label: protocol_rank_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies when a deterministic protocol partitions the same matrix into at most 2^{D_pi(g)} monochromatic rectangles.

equations.label: restricted_transfer
equations.latex: \bigl[\operatorname{rank}_{F}(M_{\pi}(f))>2^{c_T(m,s)}\bigr]\ \wedge\ \bigl[\forall g\in T_s,\\ D_{\pi}(g)\le c_T(m,s)\bigr]\Rightarrow f\notin T_s.
equations.valid_when: Requires the target-preserving communication upper bound for every target function under the identical partition and size parameter.

equations.label: equality_max_rank
equations.valid_when: Valid when EQ_r compares the two sides of the audited balanced partition and F is any field.

equations.label: full_size_threshold_collapse
equations.valid_when: Valid for every fixed balanced partition because the corresponding equality function is easy and achieves maximum rank.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposed proof infers SAT_m notin SIZE(m^k) only from rank_F(M_pi(SAT_m)) > rho(m) with rho(m)<2^r, the EQ_r falsifier shows the interface is not valid for full circuits.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-specific bridge lemma plus falsifier: it promotes rank lower bounds for low-communication targets and quarantines rank as a full-SIZE(poly) route.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Balanced matrix rank is a valid lower-bound carrier only for target classes with a proved low balanced-communication or low rank-decomposition upper bound. It cannot by itself target full nonuniform SIZE(poly), since an equality slice has maximum rank and linear-size Boolean circuits.

assumptions: F is finite with fixed size q, or the route supplies a separate density theorem for real sign matrices.
The property is total on all truth tables, not only on a promise subset.
Usefulness is stated for the same target class, partition, and input length.
definitions: rank-threshold property: P_{r,a,F}={f: rank_F(M_pi(f)) >= 2^r-a}.
constructivity scale: Gaussian elimination on a 2^r by 2^r matrix costs poly(2^m)=poly(N).
largeness scale: random matrices over F_q have full or near-full rank with constant or inverse-polynomial probability for fixed q and a=O(log N).
usefulness gate: P must reject every truth table computed by the named small target class.

equations.label: finite_field_full_rank_density
equations.valid_when: Valid for uniformly random matrices over a fixed finite field with n tending to infinity.

equations.label: constructivity_cost
equations.valid_when: Applies when the full truth table is available and arithmetic over F has constant or polynomial bit cost.

equations.label: natural_property_condition
equations.latex: P_{r,a,F}\text{ useful against }SIZE(m^k)\Rightarrow P_{r,a,F}\text{ is a Razborov-Rudich natural property}.
equations.valid_when: Requires polynomial constructivity, inverse-polynomial density, and rejection of all functions in the named circuit class.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The equality matrix is in the high-rank property and in SIZE(O(m)), so the property is not useful against full polynomial-size circuits.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier audit: rank-threshold routes are not a known natural-proof escape unless they lose largeness, constructivity, or full usefulness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Over a finite field, high-rank threshold properties of truth-table matrices are poly(N)-constructive and large at standard thresholds. If additionally useful against SIZE(m^k), they become natural properties; the usefulness premise is false for full SIZE(poly) by equality.

assumptions: The target theorem is about ordinary circuits, not circuits equipped with a partition-dependent promise.
The route claims a nonuniform lower bound, so hidden advice must be counted or forbidden explicitly.
definitions: partition leakage: the proof object contains pi as advice depending on f_m rather than as a uniform part of the route.
valid transfer: the same pi is used to rank SAT_m and to upper-bound every candidate target circuit.
invalid transfer: high rank under some pi is compared with low-rank target behavior under another or unspecified partition.

equations.label: required_quantifier_order
equations.valid_when: Valid as a warning when the partition witnessing source hardness is not also certified for the target class.

equations.label: safe_quantifier_order
equations.latex: \exists\pi\,\bigl(rank(M_{\pi}(f))>R\ \wedge\ \forall g\in T,\ rank(M_{\pi}(g))\le R\bigr)\Rightarrow f\notin T.
equations.valid_when: Applies only when the partition is part of the proof certificate and the target upper bound is proved for that same partition.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A proof that reports only the maximum rank over partitions but never proves low rank for all target circuits under the maximizing partition fails the transfer certificate.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Existentially choosing a partition after inspecting the source function does not provide a target-preserving rank lower bound. The transfer must quantify over the announced partition before both the source rank and target upper bound are evaluated.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the next proposed rank route cannot state a target-wide low-rank upper bound under a fixed partition.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if the route names a restricted target class T and proves c_T(m,s)<r-o(1), giving a nonvacuous threshold rank>2^{c_T(m,s)}.
control_decision.reason: The bridge lemma is valid for protocol-restricted targets, but the full-circuit transfer is refuted by an explicit O(m)-size maximum-rank function.

dependency_updates.description: Rank lower bounds transfer quantitatively to target classes T only through a bound D_pi(g)<=c_T(m,s), yielding threshold rank>2^{c_T(m,s)}.
Finite-field rank-threshold properties are constructive and large, so if claimed useful against full SIZE(poly) they would be natural; equality shows usefulness is false.
Pure field-rank arguments are algebraic and black-box in the truth table; no nonalgebrizing feature is present unless Boolean syntax is used in a target-preserving way.
The rank calculation is a truth-table property and supplies no nonrelativizing mechanism by itself.

falsifiers: EQ_r is a concrete falsifier: it has O(m)-size Boolean circuits and rank_F(M_pi(EQ_r))=2^r for every field.
If c_T(m,s) >= r, then the transfer threshold 2^{c_T} is at least the maximum possible rank, making the route vacuous.
Choosing pi after seeing SAT_m is an advice-leakage falsifier unless the same pi also upper-bounds every target circuit.
High real sign rank, high F_2 rank, and high deterministic communication complexity are invalid as full-SIZE(poly) certificates without an additional low-protocol theorem for the target class.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: As beta increases, rank_F(M_pi(E_{r,p})) grows as 2^r=2^{beta m/2}, while circuit size stays O(m). Thus rank can be maximized by an easy language.
held_fixed_controls: The partition pi is announced before rank computation.
The field F is fixed, e.g. F_2 or R.
The target class remains ordinary nonuniform Boolean SIZE(m^k).
The construction is explicit and decidable in polynomial time.

gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch needs to test whether matrix-rank evidence distinguishes hard languages from easy high-rank gadgets, rather than merely restating a communication-complexity lower bound.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 34 isolates a valid quantitative gate: balanced matrix rank proves lower bounds only for low-communication or low-rank-decomposition targets with threshold rank>2^{c_T}. The full SIZE(poly) route fails because equality is easy and has maximum rank under the audited partition. This is route-level barrier progress, not progress on P != NP.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Audit multiparty cylinder-intersection or tensor-rank routes with the same gate: name the target class, compute the NOF protocol threshold, and test generalized equality or inner-product gadgets as falsifiers for full SIZE(poly).

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No noncircular method is known here for proving the required unrestricted aggregate lower bound above exponent eta_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D). Such a theorem is itself a strong explicit E lower bound for A_m, while weaker aggregate evidence is consistent with all rows being easy.
steps: Define the canonical image matrix with M_m<=2^{D m+o(m)} rows and 2^m columns; its entry function is A_m(j,x).
Assume for contradiction that every emitted row has circuits of size at most 2^{epsilon m}.
Build an unrestricted selector circuit for A_m by testing j against each rank and routing x into that row's circuit; size is at most M_m(2^{epsilon m}+m^{O(1)}).
Conclude that an aggregate lower bound below 2^{(D+epsilon)m+o(m)} cannot force any row to be MCSP-hard.
Conversely, if some row is 2^{epsilon m}-hard, fixing rank bits in any circuit for A_m gives a row circuit, so A_m has size greater than 2^{epsilon m}.
After padding kappa-dense source lengths and accounting for rank length, the valid extracted E lower-bound exponent is delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The bridge is valid route-level progress, not a P != NP proof. The missing source theorem must certify structural row hardness without advice, without a subthreshold ranked decoder, and without replacing unrestricted MCSP hardness by a restricted-class lower bound.

assumptions: Rows are Boolean truth tables on m input bits, so row length is N_m=2^m.
The number of distinct emitted rows satisfies M_m<=2^{D m+o(m)} for a fixed D>=0.
The aggregate decoder is computable in deterministic 2^{O((1+D)m)} time by canonical unranking and sequential emission.
Circuit lower bounds are against unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits unless a restricted class is explicitly named.
The source verifier accepts only rows intended for the carrier; existential hardness is allowed because the aggregate target contains all ranks.
definitions: source object: a canonical distinct-image family I_m={y_{m,0},...,y_{m,M_m-1}} subset {0,1}^{2^m} emitted by E-verifiable short MCSP certificates, with M_m<=2^{D m+o(m)}.
target object: the E-uniform aggregate language A(1^m,j,x)=y_{m,j}[x] on rank j and row index x, padded from kappa-dense source lengths to all target lengths.
controlled interface: ranked aggregate decoding with E-canonical unranking, no advice, no nonuniform hard-row selector, and no subthreshold random access to rows.

target-preserving condition: kappa-dense source lengths, verifier cap epsilon<=alpha_V, unrestricted circuit lower bounds, E-uniform quotient/unranking, and row truth tables interpreted as MCSP no-side witnesses at threshold 2^{epsilon m}.

equations.label: image_entropy
equations.valid_when: Valid when the image family has at most 2^{D m+o(m)} distinct rows and rank bits are part of the target input.

equations.label: all_easy_mux_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when every row has a general Boolean circuit of size at most 2^{epsilon m} and unrestricted circuits may multiplex by equality on the rank.

equations.label: aggregate_forces_row
equations.valid_when: Valid when the aggregate lower bound is for unrestricted circuits and exceeds the full selector-multiplexer upper bound for all-easy rows.

equations.label: extracted_target_exponent
equations.valid_when: Applies after kappa-dense source lengths are padded uniformly and the aggregate input length is (1+D)m+o(m).

equations.label: aggregate_certificate_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when aggregate hardness is quoted as a size exponent relative to its own input length ell_m.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the only available aggregate lower bound has exponent eta<=(D+epsilon)/(1+D), then all rows may still be 2^{epsilon m}-easy; this is a formal falsifier for that source proof.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Sharpens the low-image carrier bridge: D is not free; it lowers the extracted exponent and raises the aggregate lower-bound threshold needed to certify row hardness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a canonical low-image MCSP carrier, forcing one 2^{epsilon m}-hard row through the ranked aggregate decoder requires an aggregate lower bound above the full selector-multiplexer threshold M_m 2^{epsilon m}. Conversely, a single hard row gives the multiplexed E language a lower bound of exponent epsilon/(1+D) before kappa padding. This is a valid bridge lemma and a quantitative falsifier for under-threshold aggregate certificates.

assumptions: Rank bits can be fixed as constants in nonuniform circuits.
The MCSP threshold is measured against unrestricted circuits on the row's m input bits.
No hidden advice is allowed in choosing the row or decoding rank names.
definitions: ranked decoder: A_m(j,x)=y_{m,j}[x] with j in [M_m] and x in {0,1}^m.
subthreshold access: a circuit family for A_m of size at most 2^{epsilon m-o(m)} measured in the source row parameter m.
MCSP no-side threshold: the claim that some emitted row has circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m}.

equations.label: rank_fixing
equations.valid_when: Valid when the same aggregate circuit is available uniformly over ranks and rank bits may be hardwired as constants.

equations.label: decoder_refutes_no_side
equations.valid_when: Valid when the asymptotic slack is below the declared MCSP threshold and circuits are unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Exhibit a ranked decoder or restart/checkpoint scheme of size below 2^{epsilon m-o(m)}; then the source is invalid, not merely unproved.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Provides a concrete falsifier for proposed bounded-image carriers with efficient rank access.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Any subthreshold circuit for the ranked aggregate decoder refutes the MCSP no-side source: fixing the rank bits gives circuits for every emitted row. Thus low image entropy is harmless only without efficient ranked random access.

assumptions: The target MCSP predicate measures unrestricted circuit complexity unless the source model is changed.
Known restricted lower bounds often fail to survive unrestricted selector multiplexing.
The bridge may still be useful for a restricted-class side target, but that is a different route.
definitions: restricted aggregate lower bound: a theorem proving A_m notin K[s] for a named class K such as AC0, formulas, or low-depth threshold circuits.
row target: MCSP no-side hardness against unrestricted SIZE[2^{epsilon m}], unless explicitly weakened to K-row hardness.
closure requirement: constants, equality on rank bits, and M_m-way selector ORs must preserve the class parameters used in the lower-bound statement.

equations.label: class_mux_obligation

equations.label: general_target_requirement
equations.valid_when: Requires the aggregate lower bound to be against unrestricted circuits, because MCSP row hardness is an unrestricted SIZE statement.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the proof only lower-bounds A_m for AC0, formulas, or another non-closed class, quarantine it unless the target is explicitly weakened.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Separates genuine MCSP carrier transfer from restricted lower-bound evidence that cannot preserve the target.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A lower bound for the aggregate decoder against a restricted class K transfers to row hardness only if K is closed under rank fixing and the all-easy-row multiplexer remains inside K with the declared size/depth parameters. Otherwise the result is not target-preserving for general MCSP.

control_decision.pivot_test: If every proposed source either has a subthreshold ranked decoder or requires proving C(A_m)>2^{(D+epsilon)m} for an explicit E function with no extra structure, pivot away from MCSP carriers.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if a no-advice, E-uniform, cap-compatible source with D=o(1) or fixed small D proves some accepted row has complexity >2^{epsilon m} without an unrestricted aggregate lower bound of comparable strength.
control_decision.reason: The bridge is now quantitatively sharp, but general aggregate lower bounds above eta_force look as hard as the desired lower-bound target. Search should focus on D near 0 structural row-hardness certificates, not on broad aggregate lower-bound slogans.

dependency_updates.description: Carrier usefulness now depends on image entropy D and aggregate forcing threshold eta_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D), not merely on low accepted entropy.
dependency_updates.status: valid bridge, source theorem still missing

dependency_updates.description: The multiplexed E target obtains exponent delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) from one hard row; aggregate lower bounds below M_m2^{epsilon m} do not certify that row.
dependency_updates.status: valid after kappa padding and E-uniform unranking

dependency_updates.description: Canonical unranking must be E-uniform but not realized by subthreshold ranked circuits; otherwise rank fixing destroys MCSP no-side soundness.
Restricted-class aggregate lower bounds and dense constructive salt repairs are outside the valid unrestricted MCSP transfer unless closure and non-largeness are proved.

falsifiers: falsifier: a ranked aggregate decoder of size <=2^{epsilon m-o(m)} makes every emitted row MCSP-easy at the claimed threshold.
falsifier: an aggregate lower bound with exponent eta<=(D+epsilon)/(1+D) cannot force a hard row, since the all-easy selector circuit remains possible.
falsifier: nonuniform choice of a hard row gives only an advice-dependent language and is not a valid E-uniform target.
falsifier: superlinear certificate length or noncanonical quotient unranking breaks E canonicalization before the carrier reaches the target.
falsifier: using a restricted-class lower bound for A_m without selector-closure does not preserve unrestricted MCSP hardness.
falsifier: adding dense random salt to raise image entropy risks a large constructive property and re-enters the natural-proofs obstruction.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: As D increases, the forcing threshold eta_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D) rises from 0.1 to 0.28 to 0.4, while the extracted exponent delta<epsilon/(1+D) falls from 0.1 to 0.08 to about 0.066. Thus bounded image entropy is only useful when D is very small and the source proof is genuinely structural.
held_fixed_controls: unrestricted circuit MCSP threshold 2^{epsilon m} with epsilon=0.1
E-uniform canonical unranking and sequential emission, with no advice
kappa=1 source length density and padding discipline
verifier cap alpha_V=1/2, so epsilon is cap-compatible
aggregate target uses rank bits plus row index bits, not a nonuniform selected row
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The route now depends on the exact tradeoff between image entropy D, source threshold epsilon, and the aggregate lower-bound exponent. A concrete parameter sweep exposes whether low-image carriers help or merely move the lower-bound burden to A_m.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: For each m, let a sequential verifier accept a canonical set of M_m=2^{D m} certificates whose distinct outputs form an M_m by 2^m truth-table matrix; study the aggregate entry function A_m(j,x) with epsilon=0.1, kappa=1, and verifier cap alpha_V=1/2.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: Before this intuition can enter the proof queue, provide either an unrestricted aggregate lower bound above 2^{(D+epsilon)m+o(m)} or an independent non-natural row-hardness certificate, plus E-uniform quotient unranking and proof that no subthreshold ranked decoder exists.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: image entropy rate D, tested at D=0, D=1/4, and D=1/2 while keeping the row threshold fixed.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 34 converts the ranked-decoder concern into an exact threshold theorem. Low distinct-image entropy D costs twice: it reduces the extracted E exponent to epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) and raises the aggregate lower bound needed to force row hardness to (D+epsilon)/(1+D). The route remains valid but only with a very small-D, cap-compatible, non-natural source or a genuinely unrestricted aggregate lower bound; otherwise the aggregate method is circular or falsified.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Instantiate a D=0 or D=o(1) canonical source candidate and audit whether its verifier can prove row hardness structurally while all ranked decoders require size >2^{epsilon m-o(m)}; reject it immediately if the proof reduces to counting images or to restricted-class aggregate hardness.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
